audit_findings.title: Uncapped separation indemnities are absent from the equity bridge
audit_findings.mechanism: Any probable indemnification obligation not already accrued or captured through owner-earnings cash payments requires a liability deduction from the equity bridge or explicit near-term OE deductions.
audit_findings.evidence: The Separation Agreement provides for indemnification obligations (for uncapped amounts, reduced by any insurance proceeds or other third-party proceeds that the party being indemnified receives) designed to make us financially responsible for substantially all liabilities, subject to certain exceptions, that may exist relating to our business activities, whether incurred prior to or following the completion of the Kenvue IPO.
audit_findings.explanation: The uncapped contractual exposure and existing Zantac indemnification demands are demonstrated, but the record provides neither asserted amounts nor the portion already accrued. The omitted incremental liability is therefore a possibility rather than a demonstrated valuation error, and its materiality cannot presently be established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain a matter-by-matter schedule of J&J demands, amounts asserted, probability assessments, recorded accruals, insurance or third-party recoveries, and expected payment timing; then rerun the bridge with the probability-weighted amount not otherwise captured in OE.

audit_findings.title: Direct international talc liabilities may exceed recorded accruals
audit_findings.mechanism: Unaccrued defense costs, settlements, or judgments would reduce future OE or require a direct equity-bridge liability deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company will, however, remain responsible for all liabilities on account of or relating to harm arising out of, based upon, or resulting from, directly or indirectly, the presence of or exposure to talc or talc-containing products sold outside the United States or Canada.
audit_findings.explanation: Kenvue's responsibility for non-U.S./Canadian talc claims is demonstrated, and the latest filing reports group proceedings in the United Kingdom and Scotland plus an Australian representative proceeding. However, Kenvue states that it cannot estimate either likelihood or magnitude, and the disclosed record does not identify claim counts, accruals, insurance coverage, or expected losses. Materiality therefore remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Obtain jurisdiction-level claim counts, alleged injuries, defense spending, settlement history, insurance limits, recorded accruals, and counsel's probability ranges; rerun the valuation with low, central, and high uncovered-liability cases.

audit_findings.title: The 2023 owner-earnings observation is not a clean standalone-company year
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; the $1,558.1m anchor is $203.4m, or 11.5%, below 2025 OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Standalone adjustments change the 2023 OE observation and therefore the three-point log trend used to set the anchor; taxes, interest, working capital, and recurring corporate costs may also affect normalized OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Accordingly, this information may not necessarily reflect what our financial condition, results of operations, or cash flows would have been had we been an independent, publicly traded company during the periods presented or what our financial condition, results of operations, and cash flows may be in the future, primarily because of the following factors:
audit_findings.explanation: The mixed carve-out and consolidated basis for 2023 is demonstrated, but the standalone adjustment is not quantified. Because the anchor is derived from only three volatile observations, a meaningful 2023 revision could alter it. Direction is mixed: omitted standalone costs would reduce 2023 OE, but lowering the first observation in this down-then-up series can raise the fitted 2025 trend value, while tax and working-capital corrections could operate differently.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct 2023 on a fully standalone basis, including debt interest, corporate functions, transition arrangements, taxes, capital spending, and working capital; rerun the identical anchor and scenarios with the reconciled figure and disclose the sensitivity.

audit_findings.title: An approved 2026 restructuring burden is outside the historical anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $250m pre-tax expected total; $147m incurred and $86m paid through 2026 H1; a mechanical full $250m deduction equals $0.13 per share and 1.1% of $23,001m base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The uncaptured cash portion is a one-time near-term OE deduction or equity-bridge adjustment; recurring savings would enter later OE or growth only when evidenced.
audit_findings.evidence: The initiative is expected to result in pre-tax restructuring expenses and other charges totaling approximately $ 250 million in fiscal year 2026, consisting of information technology and project-related costs (approximately 59 %), employee-related costs (approximately 35 %), and other implementation costs (approximately 6 %).
audit_findings.explanation: The historical anchor excludes the approved 2026 program, so the timing mismatch is demonstrated. Nevertheless, even deducting the entire stated pre-tax cost dollar-for-dollar would reduce base value from $11.52 to about $11.40 per share and bull value from $13.50 to about $13.37, leaving both well below the $18.74 price. It therefore does not change the valuation conclusion on the filed scale.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the remaining expected charges to cash, non-cash items, tax effects, and the $59m accrued balance; rerun with only incremental after-tax cash costs not already captured, while excluding the projected $200m annual savings until realized.

audit_findings.title: The pension deficit is a senior claim not shown in the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $260m filed underfunded status; $0.13 per share and 1.1% of $23,001m base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The unfunded portion not already represented in recurring pension expense or OE is a senior-claim deduction from the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: However, the Company continues to retain the primary benefit obligation until a plan wind-up and buy-out is completed.
audit_findings.explanation: The $260m funded-status shortfall and absence of a bridge adjustment are demonstrated. A full dollar-for-dollar deduction would lower base value from $11.52 to about $11.39 per share and bull value from $13.50 to about $13.37, still far below the $18.74 price. On the filed amount, it cannot change the conclusion, although an undisclosed buy-out premium should be checked separately.
audit_findings.action: Update the funded status, required contributions, buy-out premium, settlement loss, and OE amounts already charged; rerun with only the incremental after-tax economic obligation not otherwise captured.

audit_findings.title: The full cash addition may not be distributable dollar-for-dollar
audit_findings.magnitude: $1,110m cash added, including $1,089m held by foreign subsidiaries; $0.56 per share and 4.8% of $23,001m base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Only excess, unrestricted, distributable cash belongs in the equity bridge after portfolio interest income has been removed from OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Cash and cash equivalents held by our foreign subsidiaries was $1,020 million and $1,044 million as of December 28, 2025 and December 29, 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: Foreign concentration is demonstrated, but actual restrictions, operating requirements, and tax leakage are not quantified. Even the conservative extreme of removing all $1.110bn would reduce base value from $11.52 to about $10.97 per share and bull value from $13.50 to about $12.94, still below the $18.74 price. Thus this cannot change the present valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Determine latest-quarter cash by legal entity, restricted balances, minimum operating cash, local distribution limits, and withholding or repatriation taxes; rerun the bridge using only verified excess distributable cash.
